title: How I made my dragon boss
author: hyphen_ai
selftext:
Today I made the underworld boss for my game: a fire dragon that, when you beat it, gets dragged into the ground by giant skeleton hands and comes back up as a bone dragon. The video is the end result.

I did it all in Claude Code with the Voidless MCP (my own tool). Opus 5.5 wrote the initial prompts and Fable 5.2 refined the animations.

It started with one message to Claude:  
"Start designing a boss for the underworld. It will be a dragon. Two phases. First the full dragon, second one is a skeleton version of it, only bones. Flies around, shoots fire. Have wings separate if needed but we want good flapping."

Claude generated a concept image for each phase first, and once I said the design looked good it made the 3D models. Because of the flapping, it generated the body with "NO wings, four strong legs", so it rigs like any four-legged creature, and each wing as its own model ("a single large dragon bat wing, spread fully open and flat, seen from above"). The wings attach at the shoulder and flap in code. It also made tail pieces, a rib bone for the bone dragon to drop on you, and "a giant skeletal arm and clawed hand reaching straight up out of the ground". 9 models in all, every prompt ending in the same style line so they match the rest of the game.  
Each animation was one sentence, like "spits a fireball while hovering: pulls its head back, then snaps its neck forward with the jaws opening wide in one quick strike". That gave fly, breathe fire, land and spit, plus presets for idle, hurt and death.

Then came about 12 rounds of me watching recordings and telling Claude what looked off.  
"The mouth is open always, should be closed except when breathing flames." It added a jaw bone to both dragons.

"The dragon falls over before transforming. Have it get pulled into the ground by the bone hands instead." That's where the hands came from.  
"The wings aren't actually attached, floating near the flames." It moved them onto the shoulder blades. Since the wings are separate models, that was a small change, not a new dragon.  
"The fire breathing is coming out of the nose, not the mouth." The bone at the end of the head was the tip of the snout, so now the mouth is worked out from the jaw hinge.

The tail took the longest. "Maybe the tail should be split up like the serpent" got us separate tail pieces, but you could see every join. Merging them into one mesh fixed that, then: "the tail colour is more purple than black", "tail not right still, maybe it's just the model and texture". That last guess was right. It went back to the dragon's own tail and rigged it in code, and now it matches because it's the same model.

The fire and the bone dragon's collapse went the same way. "The fire breathing and fireballs look bad and not aligned with the art" swapped the pixel art fire sprites for 3D cartoon fire in the dragon's lava colours. "Mid fight the bone dragon was laying on its side" and "the rebuild isn't smooth, it just appears back to its full self" turned into this: now it bursts into a heap of bones with its heart glowing for your sword, then the bones fly back and it pulls itself together. The third time, it falls apart for good.

There's still room for refinement and adjustments, but this is where it's at for now. Happy to answer any questions about the flow.
